previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder, hypertension, and depression presented with abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting for several days. She had not been adjusting her sliding scale insulin due to a broken glucose meter and was only taking long-acting insulin. She was found in severe diabetic ketoacidosis with a glucose of 1162, pH of 7.06, and anion gap of 54. She was treated in the ICU with IV fluids, an insulin drip titrated up to 15 units/hour, and electrolyte management. Her course was complicated by transient hypotension requiring brief pressor support, acute kidney injury likely pre-renal from dehydration, and demand ischemia evidenced by ST depressions and a troponin peak of 0.28. She had a transient need for IV dextrose due to hypoglycemia during transition to subcutaneous insulin. Her kidney function improved with creatinine decreasing to 0.6, and she was restarted on lisinopril with addition of amlodipine for blood pressure control. She was discharged home with services on a reduced glargine dose, sliding scale insulin, aspirin, and close follow-up arranged with endocrinology, cardiology, and her outpatient substance use program.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with a PMH T1DM c/b neuropathy, retinopathy, and multiple 
admissions for DKA, hx etoh abuse, depression and hypertension 
presenting with DKA. 

# DKA: Patient initially admitted to the MICU for DKA in the 
setting of leukocytosis, hypotension and hypothermia with 
profound anion gap metabolic acidosis.  Of note, patient with 
history of poorly controlled T1DM c/b 
neuropathy/retinopathy/nephropathy due to poor non-adherence and 
multiple recent hospitalizations for DKA. Patient was initially 
placed on insulin gtt and then transitioned to Lantus per 
___.

# NSTEMI: In the ICU, patient was found to have peaked T-waves 
in the setting of hyperkalemia in the setting of DKA, and also 
found to have lateral ST depressions. Patient's cardiac enzymes 
were trended, and cardiology was consulted given likely CAD. TTE 
without wall motion abnormalities and demonstrated hyperdynamic 
LVEF, with mid-gradient squeeze. Patient was also placed on 
maximal medical treatment including atoravastatin, aspirin, and 
metoprolol (initially held in the setting of hypotension) and 
later resumed once pressor requirements were weaned. Due to 
likely type 1 NSTEMI and significant history of medication 
noncompliance, Cardiology deferred any further studies for risk 
stratification and felt that patient was not a candidate for 
revascularization. 

# ___: Patient was found to have elevated ___ with creatinine of 
2.8 (admission 1.0), likely thought to be pre-renal in the 
setting of hypovolemic shock as above. Patient required 
ultrafiltration via temporary HD line.  Her renal function 
recovered with fluid resuscitation, insulin regimen, and IV 
bicarbonate.  She did not require any further dialysis at 
discharge with normalization of her Cr.  

# HTN: Patient's home antihypertensives were initially held in 
the setting of shock. Amlodipine resumed on ___ and Lisinopril 
resumed on ___.

# Anemia: Patient was admitted with macrocytic anemia, thought 
likely related to alcohol abuse. Her H/H remained stable while 
she was hospitalized. Stool guiac was negative, patient did not 
require any transfusion. Patient was started on folic acid. 

# Leukopenia: Patient had stable, mild leukopenia, likely 
variant.

# Major depresssive disorder: On admission, patient without SI, 
but with severe poor care, likely contributing to multiple DKA 
admissions over past few years. Psychiatry evaluated the patient 
with recommendation for partial psychiatry treatment program 
with dual diagnosis, which the patient and patient's family 
agreed to. Per psychiatry, patient's Effexor was tapered off 
with initiation of Zoloft on ___. Per psychiatry, discontinued 
mirtazapine in the setting of IDDM as this is an appetite 
stimulant.

# ETOH abuse: Patient was a heavy drinker for years, but 
previously denied any prior history of withdrawal, including 
seizures and DTs. Has multiple DKA episodes precipitated by EtOH 
consumption or self-care deficits. PCP was contacted and relayed 
that the pt has been set up with outpt psychiatry at ___ 
multiple times, but pt continually does not keep appointments. 
We consulted psychiatry for evaluation with plan for partial 
program psychiatry placement with dual diagnosis.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure participating in your care while you were at 
___.  You were admitted to the 
hospital for altered mental status and diabetic ketoacidosis 
(DKA) due to your type 1 diabetes.  You were admitted to the 
medical intensive care unit for treatment with IV fluids and 
insulin and your DKA resolved.  You also had a heart attack due 
to your DKA, and this was treated with medications determined by 
the cardiologists.  Your symptoms stabilized and you were able 
to be transferred out of the intensive care unit.  

While you were hospitalized, we had the psychiatry team evaluate 
you and they started you on a new antidepressant medication 
called Zoloft to treat your severe depression.  They also 
recommended that you be admitted to an inpatient psychiatry ward 
for further monitoring of your depression and alcohol abuse.

You are now medically cleared to be discharged from the 
hospital.  Please call your doctor or return to the Emergency 
Department if you have any new or worsening symptoms that 
concern you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

You have follow-up appointments scheduled with your primary care 
provider as well as your diabetes doctor, the details of which 
are below.

We wish you the very best,
-- Your ___ Care Team
